title: 3verest expands sovereign healthcare AI platform using Equinix Fabric Geo Zones
full_text:
Sovereign healthcare cloud provider 3verest says it is expanding its healthcare AI platform using Equinix Fabric Geo Zones to help keep not only patient data but also AI inference, prompts and network traffic within national borders.
In a statement provided to MySecurity Media, 3verest said the approach is intended to help hospitals, medical imaging providers and healthcare technology companies adopt AI while maintaining jurisdictional control over sensitive clinical data, including during network failover and rerouting events.
The company said it is using Equinix Fabric Geo Zones to enforce “sovereignty at the network layer”, reflecting a shift in regulatory and risk concerns from where data is stored to where AI workloads run and how data moves between connected services.
3verest said its services are used by healthcare organisations across Australia, the UK, Germany, the US, Canada and the European Union, and that it is extending its platform to support cross-border expansion while keeping workloads within local sovereign boundaries.
Scott Crawford, founder and CEO of 3verest, said: “Healthcare doesn’t need another cloud. It needs infrastructure built around sovereignty from the ground up. The industry has spent years asking where data is stored, but AI changes the question to where intelligence runs. Patient imaging, clinical prompts, and AI inference must remain inside the jurisdiction, not just the archive. Equinix gives us the global digital infrastructure to build sovereign healthcare clouds consistently across multiple countries, while Fabric Geo Zones extends those guarantees to the network itself. That means our customers can adopt AI with confidence, knowing sovereignty is designed into every layer of the platform, not added afterwards.”
Equinix vice president of digital interconnection Arun Dev said the sovereignty problem increasingly involves network paths across multiple providers, not just data residency settings within a single cloud environment.
Dev said: “AI is fundamentally changing what sovereignty means. Organisations must now govern not only where data is stored, but how it moves between clouds, applications, and AI services. Sovereignty cannot be a setting inside a single cloud. It must be enforced at the network layer across every provider and every connection. That’s exactly what Fabric Geo Zones delivers. 3verest demonstrates how healthcare organisations can embrace sovereign AI while maintaining the security, compliance and operational resilience required for highly regulated clinical environments. The same principle applies to other sovereignty-critical sectors, including financial services, where data control, regulatory compliance and operational continuity are equally non-negotiable.”
According to the release, 3verest’s healthcare AI platform includes Bifrost, described as a sovereign AI environment combining GPU infrastructure, retrieval-augmented generation, AI models and managed AI services; Forge, a developer platform built on Firecracker micro-VM technology; and Heimdall, described as a control layer between healthcare applications and AI models that routes prompts and applies guardrails within a sovereign boundary.
Equinix said Fabric Geo Zones is designed to keep traffic within defined geographic boundaries across interconnected clouds and providers. The company said the capability is available across its global footprint, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, the UK, the US and the European Union.
